Alex:  I stayed until the very end of the festival and really enjoyed the final performance. The stage was full of lights and fireworks, and the atmosphere was unforgettable. Earlier, I had some trouble getting there because the traffic was terrible and the buses were crowded. Still, once I reached the venue, I forgot about all the problems. Nadia:  I usually avoid festivals, but this time I decided to go. Unfortunately, I didn’t enjoy it much. The sound system was weak, the program felt disorganized, and then it started raining heavily. Frahan: I loved the energy of the music. One band on the first night was so good that I couldn’t stop singing along. However, everything was extremely expensive. Overall, the setting of the festival was what impressed me the most.

Four people respond in the comments section of an online magazine article about FESTIVAL VER 1 ƯU TIÊN . Read the texts and then answer the questions below.

NADIA This is my first time going to a concert, and the experience was quite mixed. During the first two days. The music was rather ordinary, and the event would have been far more enjoyable if there had been just a little sunshine to brighten things up. Luckily, the last day completely changed my impression, as I finally got to see my favorite singers. Meeting them and enjoying the performances made the whole trip memorable and truly special.

 

COBRA I attend music festivals every year, and over time it has become something of a personal tradition, I really enjoy the energetic atmosphere where people come together to share music and excitement. This particular festival, however, felt quite different from what I am used to. The weather conditions were less than perfect, though it didn't bother me that much, as I have enjoyed festivals in the rain before. The venue was moderately convenient and the performances themselves were rather unremarkable. To be honest, I doubt I will choose to come back in the future.

 

FRAHAN I don't like one particular type of music being played at festivals, as I much prefer a variety of genres to enjoy and dance to. Luckily, this event truly lived up to what I was hoping for. The songs and melodies were absolutely impressive. leaving a strong impression on me. Although there was some rain, I actually felt it made the atmosphere even more vibrant and fun. One drawback, however, was the ticket price was quite high, which many students, including me, found difficult to afford.

 

ALEX My band and I were invited to play at this festival, and we delivered the kind of performance our audience has come to expect from us. The show turned out to be truly memorable, not only because of the energy on stage but also because some of our former members and past collaborators were present. It felt great to reconnect with them and share stories after the performance. The atmosphere overall was very positive, and the crowd seemed to enjoy every moment. The only real challenge was that the venue was located quite far from the main road, which made moving our instruments and equipment rather inconvenient.

Four people respond in the comments section of an online magazine article about EXTREME SPORT. Read the texts and then answer the questions below.

Leon

I don't usually like sports, but once I tried sea diving at the invitation of my friends. I fell in love with this sport ever since my first attempt. Extreme sports can be very dangerous; therefore, before I decided to take it up as a hobby, I made sure that I fully understood all the guidance from my expert trainers, who have years of experience. This helped me improve myself and feel more confident.

Mark

Some people like jumping out of aeroplanes or exploring the sea. I'm a pilot, and I have never understood why people would throw themselves into such danger. I once tried an extreme sport and realised I was right from the beginning. My job is already overwhelming and involves enough risky activities. Now, I prefer something more casual, such as baseball or volleyball.

Ian

As a child, I used to play sports because they were part of our school curriculum. I mean, whose school isn't? However, I have never enjoyed those activities. Some students are naturally gifted, as they have strong physiques and are able to endure long running sessions; however, not everyone is the same. For me, these lessons were rather a waste of time, as I preferred staying indoors and reading books.

Ana

Doing free-diving requires a lot of patience and effort to become proficient. I live far away from the sea, so it is even more difficult for me. I can only do it a few times a year, which is never enough to satisfy my passion. When I was younger, I even practised holding my breath under the shower to imagine what it would be like to breathe underwater. Once I am in the water, I feel at home. I am surrounded by various types of fish and can almost touch them.

queries.text:
Four people respond in the comments section of an online magazine article about EXTREME SPORT VER 2. Read the texts and then answer the questions below.

Person A

I had never tried any extreme sports before. One day, my friend, who was training to become a professional skydiver, invited me to join him. At first, I was really nervous when I had to jump out of the plane, and for a few seconds, I felt both scared and unsure of myself. It is crucial to perfect these skills again and again until we feel completely confident. Once I was flying freely in the sky, I suddenly felt relaxed and excited at the same time. The wonderful view above the clouds gave me a unique sense of freedom. After finishing my first skydiving experience, I realized that I truly liked extreme sports and I would be very happy to do them again in the future.

Person B

I have rarely taken part in extreme sports because I know they usually need both time and money. However, last summer I decided to go underwater diving. It was one of the most wonderful experiences of my life. When I was swimming below the surface, I could touch many beautifully coloured fish moving gracefully around me. I felt completely amazed by the beauty of nature under the sea and realized how relaxing it was just to watch these creatures in their own environment. I believe underwater sports are truly great, and I think we should take part in them more often.

Person C

I work as a pilot, and my job is already very challenging and exciting every single day. For that reason, I feel that extreme sports are not necessary for me. I do not want to spend my free time taking part in dangerous activities that could add extra risk to my life. However, I still wanted to do something healthy, so I decided to try swimming and basketball instead. Both of these traditional sports turned out to be fantastic choices. When I swim, I feel refreshed, and my whole body becomes stronger. Playing basketball with friends also gives me energy and makes me feel relaxed after a long flight. These activities are much safer than extreme sports but still very enjoyable. I can honestly say that I do not regret choosing them, because they help me stay both fit and happy without needing to take unnecessary risks.

Person D

I have never been interested in playing extreme sports because I don’t like the idea of putting myself in danger just for fun. For me, there are so many safer ways to stay active and enjoy life without having to jump out of a plane or climb a mountain. I always prefer simple and relaxing activities such as going for a walk in the park or practicing yoga at home. These activities make me feel healthy and calm at the same time. After a long and tiring day at work, I like lying down on my bed or sofa, reading a book that I enjoy.

Chris: When I was young, I really enjoyed playing board games. Now, in order to limit my kids' time on the computer, I often spend time playing with them. Jan: As a child, I didn't like going outside, so I chose reading books as my form of entertainment. The pages of the books gave me knowledge and imagination. Later, when I grew up, I started to enjoy modern games with colorful graphics, which help me relax and also boost my creativity.

Olia: When I was young, I loved outdoor activities. I remember on rainy days, I would sit by the window, staring outside, hoping the rain would stop. At those times, my mother usually gave me paper and a box of crayons. I really loved drawing and often did it at home whenever the weather wasn't good.

Four people respond in the comments section of an online magazine article about CAREER CHOICE- JOB AND TRAINING - JOB AND SCHOOL. Read the texts and then answer the questions below.

Antoni: When I first graduated from school, I wasn’t sure what to do, so I joined several volunteer programs with different companies and organizations to gain experience. I really enjoyed volunteering because it helped me decide on a career path and gave me many valuable lessons. I also believe I was able to make a difference through my work.

Muha: Back in school, I already knew I wanted to become a teacher, so I didn’t need to try other jobs. I decided to study education at university, which is free in my country. Last summer, I did some practical training in local schools, and it was extremely helpful for my future career.

Oksa: When I was young, I used to help my neighbor, a plumber, with simple jobs like measuring pipes, loosening screws, and handling tools. It felt very natural for me to learn that kind of work, so later I studied for two years at university to become an electrician. Now, I’ve learned that there are shorter courses available in this field, and I regret not choosing that option instead.

Javier: After graduating, I found it really difficult to get a job. I applied to many companies, but none accepted me because I lacked experience. Eventually, I found work at a gaming company that allowed me to work from home. It didn’t affect my daily schedule — I worked at night while my colleagues worked during the day — and that arrangement suited me perfectly.

Four people respond in the comments section of an online magazine article about VOLUNTEERING. Read the texts and then answer the questions below.

A
 I prefer donating money rather than doing hands-on volunteering. Donating online is quick and fits my schedule, and I like that NGOs can use the funds where they need them most. Sometimes I worry that money alone isn’t enough, but usually I feel confident that a financial contribution is the most effective way I can help. I also appreciate receiving updates showing how the donations were spent.

B
 I spend most of my volunteering time in my own neighbourhood. I help organise community clean-ups, run local food drives and coordinate small events at the community centre. Doing this has improved my leadership and planning skills, which later helped me when I applied for jobs. It’s often tiring, but the connections I’ve made with neighbours and local businesses make it worthwhile.

C
 My volunteering focuses on preserving local traditions. I teach children how to make traditional crafts and I help set up cultural festivals that celebrate regional music and dance. It’s rewarding to see younger people take pride in their heritage, and these activities strengthen our community identity. We often work with small museums and elder volunteers who share stories and techniques.

D
 I usually choose physically demanding volunteer projects, like building houses or restoring trails. The manual labour is tough, but I’ve noticed real physical benefits — I feel fitter and more energetic. I once joined a volunteer programme abroad that let me travel to several countries while working on construction sites; it was an excellent chance to see new places and add international experience to my CV.
